title: Halve head dim: 4 heads -> 8 heads (HEAD_DIM 128 -> 64)
description: HEAD_DIM 128 -> 64, so model_dim stays 512 but n_head/n_kv_head go 4 -> 8 with head_dim 64; nothing else changed.
reflection: NEGATIVE: val_bpb 0.999863 vs baseline 0.997358, i.e. 0.0025 worse. The comparison is clean: parameter count identical (50.3M both), peak VRAM 22.7GB both, and the run actually got slightly MORE compute (418.0M tokens / 3189 steps / MFU 33.56% vs 412.6M / 3148 / 33.12%), so the whole gap is quality per token, not throughput. Conclusion for the group: at model_dim 512 head WIDTH beats head COUNT; 4x128 is better than 8x64 and the axis points the other way, if anywhere. Do not re-buy HEAD_DIM 64 or 32. Two caveats worth recording: (a) this is a single run and round 0 showed run-to-run spread of ~0.0009 on identical configs, so 0.0025 is real but only ~3x the noise floor; (b) head_dim also sets the rotary channel count (32 freqs at 64 vs 64 freqs at 128), so this test conflates head count with positional-encoding resolution -- part of the loss may be rotary, not attention capacity. Given the batch axis is flat and the head axis is negative, the untouched high-value regions are now model shape (DEPTH/ASPECT_RATIO), the value-embedding budget (~67M params, most of the model, for zero matmul FLOPs), and the fp32 logits path (17GB tensor, prime suspect for the 33% MFU).
